There is no intervening e-m-i sequence or hyphen as in the expanded semi-finie candidate. The same short form recurs at M0313.

A tall narrow loop at the left survives, followed by a short upright/low joining stroke. The long horizontal deletion merges with the middle and reaches terminal up/down strokes at the right. The surviving beginning could support de or le, but the cancelled bodies do not yet distinguish them securely.

Before dense, the abbreviation begins with a long descending f stroke and narrow return, then a compact lower loop beneath a second rising stroke, and a final steep upright/return. These small connected components are compressed but visible above and apart from the underline; they support the abbreviated fblt without expanding it.

The word before fermé has a large hooked initial group, a low extended joining stroke, an oblique terminal stem and a smaller raised crossed stroke consistent with an abbreviated final t.
